roadmap_item: F3 (ring 1) — ambient fill; shadows stop crushing to black. Commissioned by corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1.md remedy R3, named by 3 of 5 blind judges.
state_note: DELIVERED, NOT JUDGED. The shader is real and the evidence is paired, on hardware, with a watched control. No critic has read it. `done` requires independent judgement (CLAUDE.md 0c) and this is not that.
baseline_pinned_reason: HAZARDS.md #12 — HEAD is not the baseline. Verified this turn by command, not memory: `git log --oneline eafd1316 -1` is 'Roadmap: F2 is delivered on stills alone, and the directive asks for motion', so F1 and F2 are ALREADY IN the baseline; `git diff eafd1316 HEAD -- game/src/render/post/composite.js game/src/render/renderer.js` is 86 insertions / 1 deletion and is F3 and nothing else. The tear-down therefore removes F3 and leaves F1 and F2 standing. Those two files as they stood at that sha are committed at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F3-AMBIENT-FILL/baseline-src/, so the control is rebuildable on a GPU Pod with no .git — which is how the hardware control was actually built.
could_not_do: **THE HEADLINE IS A FALSIFICATION OF MY OWN PIECE, AND IT SURVIVED.** The delete-the-fix control on an RTX A4500 came back RED and was right to. The instrument this piece had been using captured GI-off then GI-on and compared. Run against the pinned pre-F3 tree — where the shader is physically absent and setVisualFeature('giFill') throws — it still produced p10_luma 4.641 -> 14.353, against the head tree's 4.641 -> 15.001. **9.712 of the 10.360 'improvement', 93.7% of it, is reproduced by a tree with no fix in it.** The first capture is identical on both trees to three decimals; only the second diverges. The block design was measuring capture ORDER. SwiftShader reproduces the same 93.7% independently, so it is not a driver artefact. This is RULES rule 6's third and worst shape — an inert-looking fix whose number moves the right way anyway — and nothing except the delete-the-fix control would have caught it. Every number this piece reported before that point is void; the instrument was rebuilt to be paired and the piece re-measured from scratch.

**THE MECHANISM OF THAT CONFOUND IS UNIDENTIFIED, AND MY FIRST EXPLANATION FOR IT WAS WRONG — I MEASURED IT AND IT FAILED.** I proposed that the scene warms up and the first capture catches it cold. A 13-sample curve on an RTX A4500, GI held off, taken from the teleport onwards, is FLAT: p10_luma 14.297 at frame 4 and 14.300 at frame 600, total range 0.014 luma, shadow_levels 33 at every one of the thirteen samples. There is no scene-age drift. And in the SAME process, minutes later with the world over a thousand frames old, the two-still arm still returned 4.641 — so world age neither causes the dark reading nor prevents it. What actually separates them, from three measurements: teleport -> pose camera -> 4 frames reads 14.297; teleport -> 90 frames -> pose camera -> 30 frames reads 4.641; teleport -> 90 frames -> pose camera -> 240 frames reads 14.287. The dark reading appears only when the camera is JUMPED IN AN ALREADY-RUNNING WORLD AND MEASURED TOO SOON AFTER THE JUMP. Something re-converges after a camera move, is settled by 240 frames and plainly is not by 30. I did not identify what. The world clock was the obvious suspect and is ruled out BY MEASUREMENT rather than argument: a live probe shows it advancing 9.000 -> 9.0222 hours over 240 frames (40 seconds of game time, nowhere near enough sun movement to triple a shadow floor) and shows pauseClock(true) stopping it dead.

MY FIRST NULL-CONTROL METRIC (falloff_ratio = p90/p10) WAS THE WRONG OPERATIONALISATION OF 'DIRECTIONAL FALLOFF', FOUND BY RUNNING IT. A flat lift matched to the fix scored a HIGHER ratio than the fix (4.00 vs 3.46), because the ratio rewards moving the lit end up alongside the shadow floor — which is the flattening itself. Replaced by a direct lit-end-movement comparison at matched shadow floor; falloff_ratio kept as reported, non-gating context.

THE NULL CONTROL'S MATCHING CHECK WAS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, ALSO FOUND BY RUNNING IT. It demanded the flat lift's shadow floor match the fix's within 0.5 luma; an 8-bit additive lift is quantised to whole levels (round(px+K) = px+round(K) for integer px), so the achievable values are one luma apart. Worse, bisecting over real K converged onto the discontinuity itself and the applied lift became whichever side floating point landed on — which made the algebraic cross-check disagree with the frame it was predicting (4.2986 predicted vs 4.4105 measured). Fixed by searching integers only; the prediction now agrees to 1e-4 and the check requires the control to receive at least the fix's lift and at most one quantum more.

`g.h()` FROM tools/lib/browser.mjs DOES NOT THROW ON AN IN-PAGE ERROR — it calls die() and exits the process (EXIT 12, HARNESS_ERROR). The first delete-the-fix arm wrapped it in try/catch to detect the fix's absence; that is dead code and the control run died instead of recording the absence. The evaluate has to happen inside the page. Worth knowing for anyone writing a control that expects a harness call to be missing.

THE ORBIT AND PAN SWEEPS WERE BLOCK-ORDERED TOO and inherited the same confound; symptom, on hardware: at the SAME orbit angle the two blocks' first captures were 14.321 and 5.276, both outliers against their own neighbours, direction arbitrary. Rebuilt to take both arms at each pose before the camera moves.

THE SHADER-HOOK-COLLISION GATE FAILS ON THIS TREE, AND F3 IS NOT THE CAUSE — checked rather than asserted. `NO-ORPHANED-SURFACE-PASS` reports 124 of 422 materials carrying surfaceUniforms whose onBeforeCompile no longer installs them (actor.js#installWaterline overwriting installSurfaceShader, which that tool's own header names as a non-chaining hook). Run again on the pinned-baseline clone it fails **identically, 124 of 422**. The fog row `FOG-CHUNKS-SINGLE-OWNER` passes on both. So F3 leaves the gate exactly where it found it; the orphaned-surface failure is a live pre-existing defect and belongs to whoever owns actor material hooks. I did not fix it — it is outside this piece and inside F1/W1-30's territory.

SCOPE OF THE MEASUREMENT: one settlement (town-thorn), one pose family, 09:00, clear weather. Night, rain, interiors and other regions are unmeasured. A critic should assume the effect size is only established for this slice.

F2's KNOWN TERRAIN-FACET ARTIFACT (derivative-based normals reading every low-poly facet as its own plane) was not investigated for interaction with the fill. Unmeasured, because the confound above consumed the budget.

what_the_fix_actually_does.hardware: NVIDIA RTX A5000 — renderer string 'ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312 (NVIDIA NVIDIA RTX A5000 (0x00002231)), NVIDIA)', software_renderer=false. Both arms on ONE Pod and ONE GPU; the control run's own BOTH-ARMS-ON-THE-SAME-RENDERER check compares the two renderer strings and passes.
what_the_fix_actually_does.design: paired — one 240-frame warm-up, then GI off/on/off/on six times at a fixed pose with equal settle, so drift lands on both arms and cancels.
what_the_fix_actually_does.p10_luma_shadow_floor: +0.631 luma (14.287 -> 14.918), positive in 6 of 6 pairs, smallest +0.626, against 0.013 luma of drift across the whole GI-off series
what_the_fix_actually_does.p90_luma_lit_end: +0.215 luma — the lit end stays put, which is what separates this from a global lift
what_the_fix_actually_does.shadow_levels: 33 -> 34 in every one of 6 pairs. This is R3's own stated acceptance statistic and the one 5/5 blind pairs named the reference on.
what_the_fix_actually_does.local_contrast_med: 4.685 -> 4.325, -7.7%. THE WRONG DIRECTION, and it is cluster A's corroborating statistic. The confounded block design put this cost at ~30%; paired it is 7.7%. Both the benefit and the cost were inflated by the same artefact.
what_the_fix_actually_does.multi_angle: 8 of 8 orbit angles lift, both arms taken back-to-back at each pose: [0.623, 0.359, 0.692, 0.350, 0.218, 0.121, 0.537, 0.289]
what_the_fix_actually_does.motion: under a 1.5-degree-per-frame pan the frame-to-frame instability of the shadow floor is 0.1233 with GI on against 0.1284 with it off — it does not crawl; it is marginally steadier than the untouched scene
what_the_fix_actually_does.delete_the_fix: on the pinned-baseline clone the switch throws (the fix is torn out, not switched off), the GI-off series is identical to the head tree's, the paired lift collapses to -0.001 luma, the paired local_contrast change collapses to -0.001, and every per-angle lift is inside ±0.01: [0, -0.003, 0.003, 0.002, -0.007, 0, -0.010, -0.002]. The control is watched sitting at zero on every axis the head tree moves on, which is RULES rule 6's 'a control you have never seen fail is not evidence'.
what_the_fix_actually_does.null_control: the plausible wrong answer, not the trivial one: a flat additive lift solved to buy the SAME shadow floor moves the lit end by 11.000 luma where GI moves it by 0.121.
what_the_fix_actually_does.honest_size: +0.631 luma on a settled floor of 14.287 is a 4.4% lift, and +1 shadow level out of 33 is 3%. Anyone carrying away 'shadows are no longer crushed' is carrying away more than the evidence supports.

is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.answer: NO — not yet, and the blocker is not a fourth remedy. Do not pay five judges until the capture path is fixed. This is a ruling, reversible, with the evidence that would overturn it named below.
is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.reason_1_f3_is_too_small_to_move_a_judge: 4.4% on the shadow floor, +1 of 33 shadow levels, and it costs 7.7% of micro-contrast — cluster A's own statistic, i.e. F3 partially undoes what F1 bought. A forced-choice judge picking on gross appearance will not turn on this.
is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.reason_2_the_capture_path_is_the_real_bl: Read from the repo this turn: tools/visual/deck.mjs — which produced our side of the pack — poses its camera and then steps deck.json's capture.settle_frames, which is **12**, inside a loop that has already been running the world through previous setups; and it never calls pauseClock, which IS exposed at game/src/harness/api.js:195 while HARNESS.md 6 requires the clock pinned. Twelve frames after a camera jump in a running world is exactly the condition this piece measured as CRUSHED at thirty frames (4.641) and CLEAN at two hundred and forty (14.287). That does not prove the pack was captured dark — 12 is not 30, and the curve between them was still being measured when this was written — but it is the same condition, it is cheap to settle, and until it is settled 'crushed to a near-uniform black' has a plausible second author. Re-judging on a pack built by the same path would reproduce the artefact and tell us nothing about F1, F2 or F3.
is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.what_would_overturn_this: The camera-settle curve (`--warmup-curve --preroll 90`, built and running at reports/runpod-gpu/runs/w1-f3-camera-settle/) sampling at frame 12 with a preroll. If the shadow floor is already ~14 there, the pack was fine, cluster C stands as reported, and the question reduces to 'is 4.4% enough' — to which the answer is still no, but the cheap next step becomes a better F3 tuning rather than a capture-path fix. Equally: if a critic shows the paired lift is much larger at other times of day, in rain, or in interiors, the size argument weakens — I measured one settlement at 09:00 clear.
recommended_order: 1. Settle the camera-settle curve at frame 12 with a preroll. It is one Pod and a few cents, and it decides whether the blind pack was captured in the crushed condition.

2. If it was: give deck.mjs a longer post-camera settle and a pauseClock call (one file, cheap), re-capture our side, and re-run image-leakcheck.mjs against the same reference crops. If shadow_levels stops sweeping toward the reference on its own, R3 is already satisfied and F3 needs no rebuild.
3. Run F2's tool against a pinned pre-F2 clone, for the same reason this piece exists.

4. Only then decide whether F3 wants a stronger tuning — and if it does, the axis is the one named in could_not_do: separate 'how much to lift' from 'how much to blur', because the current shader buys its lift with micro-contrast.
is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.on_my_siblings_deferring_to_me: F2's builder and F1's critic both deferred the re-judge decision to whoever landed last. My answer is above and it is a harder no than either of them expected — but it is a no about the instrument, not about their work. F1 and F2 are untouched by this finding except that they were measured by the same tooling, which is itself worth a look.
is_it_worth_re_judging_blind.a_question_for_f1_and_f2: F2's instrument (tools/visual/w1-v2-contact-ao.mjs, read this turn) is ALSO block-ordered — one arm, then the other — which is the pattern that manufactured a 10-luma difference here. It differs in one way that probably saves it: its captureArm calls loadState('material_showcase') at the start of EVERY arm, so each arm begins from a freshly loaded fixture rather than a running world, which is the condition my curve measured as clean. I am NOT asserting F2 is confounded — I have no evidence either way and did not run it. The cheap check is to run F2's own tool against a pinned pre-F2 clone and see whether its number reproduces without the fix; that is one command and it is the same check that caught this.

evidence.citable: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F3-AMBIENT-FILL/ — README.md leads with the falsification. hw-final-a5000/ is the citable run (head + pinned-baseline control, paired, with the verdict's own two statistics); hw-paired-a5000/ is an independent repeat reaching the same conclusions; baseline-src/ is the pinned pre-F3 source so the control is rebuildable anywhere.
evidence.kept_deliberately: reports/runpod-gpu/runs/w1-f3-ambient-fill/ (RTX A4500, the block design that falsified itself) and corpus/.../sw-head + sw-deletefix (SwiftShader, the independent replication of the confound at the same 93.7%). A confound deleted once a better instrument exists cannot teach anybody anything.
evidence.landed_and_verified: every corpus artefact above was landed with `node tools/land.mjs --paths` and the tool printed `verified N path(s) against the remote blob` — HAZARDS.md 9's requirement, checked against the remote and not against `git status`.

next_step: For a critic: the claim to attack is the effect SIZE and the SCOPE, not the direction — the direction has a watched control sitting at zero. Two specific attacks worth paying for: (1) re-run --alternate at other times of day, in rain, and in an interior, since I measured one settlement at 09:00 clear only; (2) take the warm-up curve to frame 12 and settle whether the blind pack was captured unsettled, because that decides whether the whole visual programme has been judged on frames the player never sees. For the orchestrator: the capture-path fix in deck.mjs is a small, cheap piece and it blocks the re-judge.
